classification.difficultyReason: Sketch both standard curves, use their phase relationship or equal-value angles to locate both intersections, and obtain exact ordinates with the correct signs.

content.prompt: Sketch the graphs of $y=\sin x$ and $y=\cos x$ over $x\in[0,2\pi]$ on the same set of axes. Find and label the points of intersection.

answer.worked:
Sketch the standard sine and cosine curves using their quarter-cycle key points. Their equal ordinates occur halfway between $0$ and $\frac\pi2$, and one half-turn later. Thus $x=\frac\pi4,\frac{5\pi}4$.

$$\begin{align*}\sin\frac\pi4&=\frac{\sqrt2}2\\\sin\frac{5\pi}4&=-\frac{\sqrt2}2\end{align*}$$
Label both intersection coordinates on the sketch.

spec.description: Sine and cosine with both exact intersections marked and labelled.
